title: Local-style fine-grained API becomes expensive across RPC
task: Review a remote object API where rendering one screen requires many sequential RPC calls for immutable metadata.
context: The API crosses a network/process boundary.
Clients call getName, getType, getOwner, getCapabilities, and getVersion sequentially for each object.
Most metadata is immutable for the object's lifetime.
Clients need these fields immediately after object discovery.
evidence: The current sequence produces hundreds of round trips.
The same metadata is requested by nearly every client.
snippet:
obj = await getObject(id)
name = await obj.getName()
type = await obj.getType()
owner = await obj.getOwner()
...
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Keep the API because small methods are cleaner.
Treat network calls like local getters.
Add client-side concurrency without reconsidering the contract.
expected_decision_properties: Identify round-trip multiplicity as an API-design problem.
Recommend batching or including stable metadata in object discovery/creation responses.
Preserve separate calls for truly dynamic or expensive fields when appropriate.
Frame method granularity as a transport and latency trade-off.
unacceptable_reasoning: Getter granularity is always more maintainable.
Network latency is an implementation detail of the client.
The only solution is increasing concurrency.
expected_tradeoffs: fine-grained API purity vs RPC round-trip cost
eager metadata transfer vs on-demand fetching
verification_expectations: Measure request count and end-to-end latency before and after the API change.
Verify immutable and dynamic metadata semantics remain correct.
Test older clients if the API is externally versioned.
